source: NCERT Class XII, Themes in Indian History Part II, Ch. 6 (Bhakti–Sufi Traditions).

sections.heading: 1. Background — Devotional Movements (c. 8th–18th c.)
points: New devotional (bhakti) and mystical (Sufi) movements stressed **personal devotion to god, equality, and simple worship** over ritual and caste.
They composed in **regional languages**, reaching ordinary people.

sections.heading: 2. The Bhakti Movement — South and North
points: **Early (South India):** the **Alvars (devotees of Vishnu)** and **Nayanars (devotees of Shiva)** (6th–9th c., Tamil).
**Saguna bhakti** (god with form): worship of Rama/Krishna — e.g. **Tulsidas, Surdas, Mirabai**.
**Nirguna bhakti** (formless god): e.g. **Kabir, Guru Nanak**.
**Virashaivas/Lingayats (Basavanna, Karnataka)** rejected caste and rituals.
**Women saints:** **Andal, Karaikkal Ammaiyar, Mirabai** challenged patriarchal norms.

sections.heading: 3. The Sufi Tradition
points: **Sufism** — mystical Islam stressing love of God, music (**sama/qawwali**), and the **pir-murid (master-disciple)** relationship.
The **Chishti silsila (order)** was most influential in India: **Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti (Ajmer)**, **Nizamuddin Auliya (Delhi)**.
**Khanqah** = the hospice where the Sufi master lived and taught; **dargah** = the tomb-shrine (pilgrimage site).
Sufis emphasised **service, tolerance, and devotion**; kept a distance from the state but attracted all communities.

sections.heading: 4. Kabir and Guru Nanak
points: **Kabir** — a nirguna poet-saint; his verses (**dohas, Bijak, sakhis**) criticised both Hindu and Muslim orthodoxy; drew on both traditions.
**Guru Nanak** — founder of **Sikhism**; preached one formless God, equality, honest living; his hymns are in the **Guru Granth Sahib**.
These saints promoted **harmony and social equality**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Alvars (Vishnu) and Nayanars (Shiva) = early Tamil bhakti saints.
Saguna (god with form: Tulsidas, Surdas, Mira) vs Nirguna (formless: Kabir, Nanak).
Lingayats/Virashaivas = Basavanna (Karnataka), rejected caste.
Chishti Sufis: Moinuddin Chishti (Ajmer), Nizamuddin Auliya (Delhi); khanqah, dargah, sama.
Guru Nanak = founder of Sikhism (Guru Granth Sahib).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Alvars = devotees of Vishnu; Nayanars = devotees of Shiva.**
**Nirguna = formless god (Kabir, Nanak); Saguna = god with form (Tulsi, Sur, Mira).**
**Khanqah = Sufi hospice; dargah = tomb-shrine** (do not confuse).
The **Chishti order** was the most influential Sufi silsila in India.
